title: The Self-Cage: Pin the Promoted Bishop
summary: After the bishop promotion, Black must find a drawing defense while White threatens mate.

nodes.question: How can Black answer the newly promoted bishop without allowing mate?
nodes.explanation: Be6 controls g8 and uncovers the rook’s pin on Bf8. White’s king and pawns cannot move, and the bishop cannot leave the eighth rank without exposing Kh8. White is stalemated.

branches.title: Source defense: pin the promoted bishop
commentary: Begin after the source f8=B. All ten pieces are retained. Black moves next and must avoid White’s mating threat on g7.
Be6 controls g8 while clearing g8 for the rook’s pin along c8–h8. Bf8 cannot move without exposing Kh8. Kh8 has no legal flight and g4/h5 are blocked. White is not in check: actual stalemate.
branches.explanation: Be6 controls g8 while clearing g8 for the rook’s pin along c8–h8. Bf8 cannot move without exposing Kh8. Kh8 has no legal flight and g4/h5 are blocked. White is not in check: actual stalemate.

branches.title: Independent defense: remove the bishop
commentary: Test a different drawing defense independently of the source’s final pin. Capturing a promoted piece does not automatically remove a stalemate resource.
Rxf8 captures the promoted bishop. Rf8 protects Bg8, Kh6 covers g7/h7, and the white g4/h5 pawns remain blocked. Kh8 has no legal move and is not in check: actual nine-piece stalemate.

exercises.prompt: Why does Bf8 become immobile after Be6?
exercises.answer: Moving it would uncover Rc8’s attack along the eighth rank to Kh8. The bishop is pinned, while Be6 also covers g8.

exercises.prompt: Does this prove bishop promotion was the only drawing choice earlier?
exercises.answer: No. Exact verification begins after the illustrated f8=B. The earlier position and alternative promotions require their own outcome analysis.

startContext: Begin immediately after f8=B at 130 seconds, with the complete ten-piece source board: White Kh8/Bf8/g4/h5 against Kh6/Rc8/Bg8/a3/g5/g7, Black to move. This later position is exactly drawn by independent finite non-loss certificates for both sides. Black can choose Be6 for immediate stalemate. White’s certificate checks all twenty Black replies, reaching actual stalemate or actual mate; the Rc7/Bxg7+/Rxg7 source route is checked inside that certificate without claiming the intermediate Rc7 position’s exact outcome. Earlier Ne7/h5/Ng8/f7 maneuvers and the assertion that bishop promotion is the only drawing choice remain outside proof. Black is the practice side here, seeking a drawing defense after the illustrated bishop promotion.
